x: George Checkley went back to 18th losing 14 minutes on Bob Newson from 10 miles onwards. Syd Spencer walked his usual steady race. Bob Newson deservedly won the handicap off 16.30 and we had quite an enjoyable journey home.

Harry after a not very good day, finished 27th with evergreen Bob Readman 42nd, Bill True 49th, Syd Spencer 63rd and Cyril Yescombe 66th. Since this event Cyril has shown considerable improvement and looks like being an asset to the team next year.

There was a total of 46 walkers from this country including six of our members, viz; George Place, Cyril Yescombe and Syd Spencer in the Police team and Ber[illegible]ard Eglington, Jack Goswell and myself in the R.W.A. team, with Sid James and Ron Kim as attendants.

Bob Readman, Sid Spencer, Gerry Plaice and Cyril Yescombe were noticed having a steady training spin, probably discussing the advantages or disadvantages of Constabulary duties and civilian life, and Bernard Stevenson had a few behind him this time.

The handicap held in conjunction was really an excellent effort by Bill True, the handicapper, Cyril Yescombe off 28 minutes, winning by one second from Bob Newson, with Syd Spencer 3rd beating Fred Rolfe by two seconds.

Of our others, Cyril Yescombe and Harry Shields had their usual social outing, and George Place and Syd Spencer seemed to enjoy their trip round this corner of Middlesex which still has fields and trees to show something remaining of a rural atmosphere.

Sidney G.SPENCER (Middlesex)
Stirling Wakeley to win a 24 Hour Track Walk at Motspur Park in 1948 and helping fellow Belgravians, Gordon Doubleday and Syd. Spencer compete successfully in races at 100 miles and over.
In 1952 another classic route was walked, Bath to London (Chiswick) and Chelsea policeman Syd Spencer recorded a very fine 20:09:45 for badge No. 181.
